title: Our future is still a choice
description: An educational guide to choosing joyful responsible abundance, from everyday agency and shared computing to superintelligence and Australian sovereignty.

title: A first look at the whole system
description: Begin with the human question, learn the three principles, and connect everyday problems with the AI race.

title: Explore the whole system
description: Every component of the whole-system proposal, with direct links to its explanation and public projects.

title: People and practice
description: How a personal Aura, practical learning and continuity of care can help people carry their experience through life.

title: Shared capacity and ownership
description: Healthy living, time, useful work and locally owned computing give more people the means to act.

title: Evidence and public decisions
description: Follow a household bill, a legal question or a local problem through evidence, responsibility and a public response.

title: Cooperation across the world
description: Connect personal growth, AI alignment, peaceful cooperation and the proposed global festival in July 2035.

title: Superintelligence and Australian sovereignty
description: Understand the race over AI, industrial capability and authority, then explore Australia’s practical choices.

title: When intelligence becomes infrastructure
description: AI matters beyond the screen when the software, electricity, machines and authority to act become part of the same system.

title: Who owns the machinery and the decisions?
description: The race combines model developers, cloud companies, factories, investors and governments. Their figures measure different things, and their ownership structures differ.

title: How computing, robots and space could accelerate one another
description: Orbital power, reusable transport, factories, robotics and materials discovery form a possible feedback loop. The paper turns that possibility into requirements people can examine.

title: Keeping authority when software can act
description: The ability to act through tools and machines raises practical questions about permission, updates, procurement, local control and the right to challenge a decision.

title: Planning for five very different horizons
description: The paper tests conditional paths to 2027, 2028, 2029, 2031 and 2036. Its figures make assumptions visible and identify the delivery evidence to watch.

title: Making sovereignty something people can use
description: Shared local equipment, personal Auras, carefully governed connections and civic practice address different parts of the same question about who gets to act.

title: The complete sovereignty paper
description: The full reviewed paper with dated references and the method behind its conditional scenarios.

title: Explore the scale and connections
description: A transparent compute-cost calculator and an interactive tree explaining how the system’s components connect.

title: References and source documents
description: A searchable source library linking both papers, their references and the associated public projects.

title: Related public projects and repositories
description: Explore the public sites and source repositories connected with the whole-system plan.

title: Words explained
description: Plain-language explanations of the terms used throughout the plan and sovereignty paper.

title: About the work and image credits
description: Authorship, edition details, image provenance, accessibility and reuse permissions.

title: Site map
description: A complete directory of the website’s guides, interactive tools, original papers, references and projects.
